blocking_question_recorded: no incremental reparse consumer exists: Atlas re-parses every admitted file with syn on every run (no derivation is cached -- see salsa), and no performance problem motivates incremental parsing
blocking_question_status: STALE on its first clause: ADR 0008's per-artifact ExtractionCache (systemize --cache) already restricts re-extraction to changed artifacts; the second clause is the falsification below

falsification.claim: sub-file incremental reparsing (ts_tree_edit / get_changed_ranges) would materially reduce Atlas's recensus cost
falsification.method: release atlas-systemizer systemize --root . --cache <dir> on the clean tree at 7e4e88e76e: one cold run, three warm runs, then three warm runs each after appending one function to the largest non-test Rust file (core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs, 4,324 lines); wall time by perf_counter
falsification.result: FALSIFIED: re-extracting the whole edited file is indistinguishable from run-to-run noise (cold minus warm = ~3-4 s for 89 artifacts, ~40 ms per artifact on average for parse AND semantic extraction); sub-file reparsing could save at most part of one file's parse, well under 1% of a ~6 s warm run, while adding a stale-state failure class

mechanisms.mechanism: incremental parsing with edit ranges and subtree reuse
mechanisms.reason: falsified above; whole-file reparse behind the per-artifact cache is sufficient

mechanisms.mechanism: grammar-modular multi-language parsing (generated LR/GLR tables per language)
mechanisms.reason: the modular-frontend principle is already Atlas-native (adapter::source::SourceFrontend registry: 10 frontends); running third-party grammars would be a runtime dependency, not absorption, and needs the parser sandbox/resource-limit admission path that does not exist; each grammar is its own donor when a language is admitted

Atlas records a whole-file parse failure as explicit UNKNOWN obligations with a ParseFailure diagnostic; localizing it is a precision improvement with no current consumer -- recorded as a future census-precision idea, not absorbed
structural search belongs to the ast-grep (#12) and semgrep (#11) cycles

extinction.runtime_dependency: none (no Cargo edge, no FFI, no vendored code)
extinction.transitive_or_shared: none: grammar repositories were never materialized
extinction.remaining_unabsorbed_mechanisms: all four are REFERENCE_ONLY; the pinned commit, license and provenance stay recorded, so any re-read re-materializes by sha
extinction.action: git rm -r .atlas/temporary/donors/tree-sitter (618 tracked files, 6.5 MB); recoverable from history, like the souffle/datafrog/blake3 extinctions
extinction.post_delete_verification: workspace tests (donor storage integrity included), self-recensus of the tree with the donor absent (G65 recensus: census unchanged -- donors are outside census scope)

census_improvement_exposed: P4 input: ~6 s of a warm self-recensus is spent outside parsing/extraction (inventory digesting, census build, normalization, graph); incremental dependency-aware recensus must target those stages, not parsing
